cards.explanation: The answer is False. The LORD says the opposite: “Do not learn the ways of the nations or be terrified by the signs in the heavens, though the nations themselves are terrified by them.” So the nations panic, and Israel is told not to. Nobody needs to copy the person screaming at the sky.

The answer is a tree cut down from the forest. Before any silver or gold shows up, it's just wood, and a craftsman shapes it with a chisel. Something that started out standing in the woods is about to get called a god. Friends, I need a minute with that.

The answer is so it will not totter. They fasten it with hammer and nails so that it will not totter. Silver and gold all over it, and it still needs help standing up. I'd love to hear the sales pitch for that one.
The answer is carried. The passage says, “They must be carried because they cannot walk.” I get around my bakery by hopping, gold base and all. These idols can't even manage that.

The answer is that they can do no harm and no good. The LORD says, “Do not fear them, for they can do no harm, and neither can they do any good.” There's nothing to be afraid of, and nothing to hope for either. It's a scarecrow in a cucumber patch with a lot more jewelry.

The answer is none at all. The passage says that among all the wise men of the nations, and in all their kingdoms, “There is none like You…” Not one of them comes close. You can search every kingdom you want.

The answer is Tarshish. The passage says, “Hammered silver is brought from Tarshish, and gold from Uphaz…” So the passage names where the metals come from. That's a whole shipping order for something that can't walk to the door.

The answer is skilled workers. The passage says the idols' clothes are blue and purple, “…all fashioned by skilled workers.” So the outfit comes from people who know their craft. And the idol can't even hold still without nails.

The answer is living. The passage says, “But the LORD is the true God; He is the living God and eternal King.” The idols have no breath in them, as verse 14 says. The LORD is alive, and He's King forever.

The answer is that they will perish from this earth. The words say these gods “…will perish from this earth and from under these heavens.” They don't get to stay on a shelf forever. They're going away.

The answer is the waters in the heavens. The passage says, “When He thunders, the waters in the heavens roar…” It's the LORD's thunder, and the sky answers. Try getting that out of something held together with nails.
The answer is False. The passage says, “every goldsmith is put to shame by his idols.” He's put to shame, not proud. Imagine hammering away for weeks and the thing makes you look foolish.
The answer is fraud. The passage says, “For his molten images are a fraud, and there is no breath in them.” They look impressive, but nothing's behind it. All shine and no breath.

The answer is that He is the Maker of all things. The passage says, “…He is the Maker of all things…” The idols had to be made by somebody, and the LORD made everything. That's the whole gap between them.

The answer is True. The passage says, “…Israel is the tribe of His inheritance…” The LORD is called the Portion of Jacob, and Israel is His inheritance. It's a warm way to close out all that talk about idols.
